incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty INC12345 — GPU kernel alloc failures detected in pool 'serve-gpu-pool-a' (cudaAlloc retries). Alert rate 6/min. Auto-escalation threshold hit.
pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to on-call: anya (primary). Please acknowledge.
anya (oncall): acked. I'm looking. Can someone paste recent errors and whether traffic is being dropped or routed?
samir: seeing repeated logs from worker-23: `E tensorflow: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` then `KernelLaunch: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED`. Affected requests ~8% errors over last 3m.
samir: nvidia-smi snapshot (short):
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.1     |
| GPU  Name        Memory-Usage  GPU-Util  Temp |
| 0    A100-40GB   38900MiB/40536MiB   98%    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
leo: host-level OOM not obvious, but vmem on host creeping. dmesg shows `NVRM: rm_init() failed` sporadic.
ops-runbooks-bot: Runbook suggestion: 1) Isolate pool, 2) evict noisy KV-prefetch jobs, 3) scale up pool by +1 GPU, 4) fallback to quantized-variant model. Runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/gpu-alloc-failure
anya (oncall): ok doing quick mitigation: 1) Mark pool `sched-drain=true` for canary new assigns, 2) kick autoscaler to add 1 node, 3) trigger routing to fallback model variant.
infra-automation-bot: `kubectl label nodepool serve-gpu-pool-a sched-drain=true --overwrite` queued (job id 6543).
anya (oncall): samir, can you identify top noisy job ids causing high KV prefetch?
samir: top offenders (by tokens/sec): `req-8721`, `req-8810`, `batch-ctx-449`. I'll kill `req-8721` and throttle prefetch on the others.
leo: I'm attaching short trace of one failed request:
```
[2026-03-14T04:12:01Z] Worker=worker-23 pid=2145 ERROR cudaMalloc(2147483648) -> CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
[2026-03-14T04:12:01Z] stack: ml_infer::alloc_cache -> cuda_alloc_pool -> cublas::init
```
katie: Customer-impact check: only 2 customers reported degraded throughput; error rate spike matches US-west traffic. CS notified. @customer-success can you confirm outreach?
customer-success: pinged affected customers with status note. No escalations yet, asking for ETA.
anya (oncall): temporary mitigation enacted: 1) `evict` noisy jobs 2) routing flag set to `model-quant-q4f` for new sessions 3) autoscaler request submitted. Observed error rate dropping to 2/min.
ops-runbooks-bot: If kernel allocs persist after scaling, try `--kv-prefetch=off` on the worst pools and set `gpu-slab-threshold=0.75`.
samir: applied `--kv-prefetch=off` to serve-gpu-pool-a scheduler; restarted worker-23 gracefully (`systemctl restart rtw-worker@23`) — monitoring.
infra-automation-bot: Autoscaler accepted request, adding 1 x A100 node to serve-gpu-pool-a (~3m ETA).
anya (oncall): quick check of metrics: memory pressure (per-GPU) down from 96% -> 78% on average after evictions. Error rate 0.7% now.
leo: collecting core dumps + `dmesg`/`journalctl -u rtw-worker@23` and uploading to /var/artifacts/incidents/INC12345.tar.gz
anya (oncall): decision: keep pool in drain for 10m, autoscale to +1, keep fallback model routing until error rate <0.2% for 15m. If errors reappear, page infra lead.
pagerduty: INC12345 acknowledged by anya. Status: mitigated (monitoring). Escalation suppressed.
customer-success: updated customers with mitigation note; next update in 30m.
anya (oncall): monitoring window started. If anyone sees new cudaAlloc failures, ping here immediately. :eyes:
samir: will follow up with post-incident triage notes once we have artifacts.
ops-runbooks-bot: log extraction commands used: `kubectl logs -n inference worker-23 --since=30m > /tmp/worker-23.log` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY > /tmp/nvmem.log`.
anya (oncall): thanks all — keeping thread open for triage.
